subject: Post-incident assurance brief & verification request
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@finedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident assurance brief & verification request

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for your patience while our team finished the internal investigation. Attached is a concise assurance brief that covers: a high-level RCA, a minute-by-minute timeline for the event window, and the corrective actions we have committed to and the owners for each item. The attached CSV is an action ledger with owners and target dates.

Key points up front:  
- Root cause: A regression in our autoscaling decision logic combined with an unexpected model cache eviction under a high-concurrency profile. This caused increased latency and a small number of token-serving errors between 03:18–03:47 UTC.  
- Impact: ~0.7% of requests for your account experienced elevated latency; <0.05% returned 5xx errors. No data exposure.  
- Immediate fixes deployed: configuration patch to autoscaler, guard added to KV cache eviction path, and a short-term rollout to a more conservative batching profile.

What we are proposing for verification: a joint validation run of your peak workload using our verification harness (safely replayed synthetic traffic) and a 72-hour monitoring window. We will provide the harness results and the raw traces for your team to cross-check.

Can you confirm whether the week of Apr 12 works for a 60–90 min verification session? We can also provide the verification artifacts in a private S3 share if you prefer.

Attachments: redwood_rca_finedge_20270406.pdf, finedge_action_items_20270406.csv

—
Logan Wright
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@finedge.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinEdge Support <support@finedge.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-incident assurance brief & verification request

Logan —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. A few quick questions from our side before we schedule:  
1) Can you confirm the exact rollback window for the autoscaler change? We want to understand what traffic could have been rerouted and if any retries occurred on our end.
2) For the verification harness: will it simulate our customer mix (mix of short chat calls and long context generation)? We need it to reflect our 70/30 short/long split.
3) SLA credit ask: can you outline the mechanism/process for requesting credits for impacted requests? Our procurement team will need the steps.

If possible, please include Hannah on the technical call — she led our infra efforts and will want to review traces. We are tentatively available Apr 13–15 afternoons ET.

Regards,
Aisha Patel
Head of Platform Engineering
FinEdge
aisha.patel@finedge.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@finedge.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-incident assurance brief & verification request

Hi Aisha —

Thanks — quick answers below and next steps:  

1) Rollback window: the autoscaler configuration that triggered the behavior was rolled forward at 03:14 UTC on Apr 6 as part of a staged launch. We detected the anomaly at ~03:18 UTC and initiated an emergency rollback to the previous config at 03:26 UTC. The final guard was in place by 03:35 UTC; residual KV evictions resolved by 03:47 UTC. I’ve included the minute-level timeline in the attached PDF (page 2).  

2) Verification harness: yes — the harness supports weighted traffic profiles. We will model your 70/30 short/long split and run three iterations at your peak concurrency target. We will sanitize any replayed inputs and only use synthetic payloads.

3) SLA credits: our standard process is to raise a credit request via your account rep after the verification completes. I’m copying your procurement contact in a follow-up Doc; we’ll include the affected request count and the compensation calculation per your contract (Section 4.2).

Proposed times: Apr 14, 13:00–14:30 ET or Apr 15, 14:00–15:30 ET. Which works best?

Action owner table (excerpt):
- Marissa Cole: schedule verification, provide harness & traces; target Apr 14/15.
- Hannah Schmitt: supply raw traces and assist on validation run.
- Logan Wright: executive liaison and formal assurance sign-off.

Happy to sync and I can open a calendar invite once you confirm a slot.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@finedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 02:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-incident assurance brief & verification request

Aisha —

Appreciate the quick read and the clarifying questions. Apr 14 at 13:00 ET is confirmed on our side; I’ll send the invite and include a short pre-read (2 slides) that summarize the validation plan and expected outputs.  

Logistics we will deliver before the call:  
- Verification harness repo and instructions (private link).
- Raw, time-synced traces for the event window and the verification runs.  
- A one-page SLA credit request template and the sample calculation we will use.

If anything changes on your availability, ping Marissa and she’ll rebook. We look forward to walking through the findings live and delivering the verification artifacts for your records.

Best,
Logan
